rationale: C25 is a highly plausible drafting template: it has the identical title, uses the same numbered list to make several discrete changes to the customs field organization, and employs the same operative formulas for designating and revoking customs ports of entry and extending port limits. C14 is another strong precedent using the same machinery, while C13 is weaker because it reorganizes internal-revenue districts rather than customs ports.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The designation of Provincetown, Massachusetts, as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 4 (Massachusetts), is revoked.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The designation of Guayanilla, Puerto Rico, as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District Number 49 (Puerto Rico) is revoked.
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive, nearly verbatim operative formula for revoking a named customs port within a numbered customs collection district.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Pelican, Alaska, is designated as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 31 (Alaska).
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Neah Bay, Washington, is designated as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District Number 30 (Washington).
shared_material.explanation: Same sentence-level template for designating a new customs port, with only the location and district changed.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The limits of the customs port of entry of New London, Connecticut, in Customs Collection District Number 6 (Connecticut), are extended to include the territory embracing the municipality of Groton, Connecticut.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The limits of the customs port of entry of Lawrence, Massachusetts, in Customs Collection District Number 4 (Massachusetts) are extended to include the township of North Andover, County of Essex, State of Massachusetts.
shared_material.explanation: Same administrative machinery and closely parallel language for expanding the territorial limits of an existing customs port.
